To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transcription factor activity of a cell can change over time in response to intrinsic or extrinsic factors, and the transcription factor activity can change in a manner that is independent of the transcription factor concentration.

1) the use of single cell RNA-seq data to infer transcription factor binding sites is limited by the low resolution of RNA-seq, and 2) single cell ChIP-seq data is limited by the inability to accurately infer transcription factor activities.

the dynamics of transcription factor binding to the genome are highly variable among cells of the same cell type and that these dynamics can be modulated by extrinsic factors such as growth factor stimulation and cell-to-cell contact.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms that regulate gene expression and how they are affected by intrinsic and extrinsic perturbations.
understanding transcription factor regulation in terms of gene regulation.

the molecular and cellular basis of gene expression in individual cells and how it changes in response to intrinsic factors (e.g., cell cycle, differentiation) and extrinsic factors (e.g. growth factors, drugs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field is still in its infancy and that the current approaches are not yet able to provide an accurate view of how transcription factors regulate gene expression at the single cell level.
the transcriptional regulatory network is a complex system that is not easily deciphered, even with modern technology.
the field has not yet arrived at a level where we can confidently state how transcription factor dynamics are related to gene regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the transcriptional regulatory landscape of a single cell can be very complex and that it can vary greatly from one cell to the next.
transcription factors are not only important for gene expression, but also for the regulation of gene expression, and that their dynamics are important for the regulation of their own dynamics.

transcription factor activities can be modulated in many ways, and that the specific mechanisms that regulate transcription factor activities can vary from one cell to another, and from one time point to another.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the most accurate conclusions about gene regulation are likely to come from a combination of experimental approaches, and that the best approach to study gene regulation in a particular cell type will depend on the biological system being studied.
the field of transcription factor biology would greatly benefit from a more holistic and integrated approach to the study of transcription factor dynamics and gene regulation.
the field of transcriptional regulation would benefit from the development of a unified approach for studying transcription factor dynamics.
